question_text: Rule: 'Only citizens aged 18 and above may vote.' Juan is 20 years old and a citizen. Therefore:

hint_ladder.title: Tingnan ang rule conditions
hint_ladder.text: The rule: 'Only citizens aged 18+ may vote.' Checklist ng dalawang items: (1) citizen, (2) at least 18. Both must be met.

hint_ladder.title: I-check si Juan
hint_ladder.text: Juan ay citizen, so checked. 20 years old siya, above 18, so checked. Lahat satisfied.

hint_ladder.title: Diretsong apply ang rule
hint_ladder.text: Since both boxes ticked, the rule says 'may vote' – diretsong conclusion. No further kalkal.

hint_ladder.title: Piliin ang tamang sagot
hint_ladder.text: Option A matches exactly. Others either contradict (B), create doubt (C), or add extra requirement (D).

A.text: Correct. Juan satisfies both conditions, so the rule allows him to vote directly—no hidden requirements.

B.text: You might have chosen B because you hastily assumed something else disqualifies him, but both conditions are met, so 'may vote' stands.

C.text: You might have chosen C because you generalized that there might be hidden conditions, but the rule is clear and all given facts satisfy ...

D.text: You might have chosen D because you assumed registration is required, but the given rule only needs citizenship and age—no extras.

next_time_rule: Treat clear rules like checklists: if both boxes ticked, conclusion follows. Don't overthink or add extra steps. Idiretso mo lang.
deconstruct_text:
Isipin mo, sa barangay elections, may rule: 'Only citizens aged 18 and above may vote.' Parang checklist 'yan. Check box 1: citizen ba si Juan? Oo. Box 2: at least 18 years old? Oo, 20 na siya. Kaya automatic, satisfy niya conditions.

Mental Trick: 'Checklist lang, walang 'pero'. Kapag citizen at 18+, automatic may vote. Huwag mong dagdagan ng registration o kung anuman. Idiretso mo lang—Juan may vote.'
